key_insight: Machine-learning models compress quantum measurement data to rapidly supply wavefunction overlaps, accelerating quantum-classical Monte Carlo by orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Reusing learned quantum-state information reduces classical processing costs that constrain hybrid quantum simulation workflows.
method: Prepare trial wavefunctions on a quantum processor to guide classical quantum Monte Carlo.
Compress quantum measurement data into machine-learning models.
Use model-provided wavefunction overlaps during Monte Carlo simulation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports chemically accurate simulations up to 40 qubits on hydrogen chains and strongly correlated iron-sulfur clusters using measurements from Google's Willow processor.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify training costs or how overlap-prediction errors affect accuracy beyond the demonstrated systems.
paper_title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
